propositions: The ADR-promised byte-total backstop trigger does not exist; _gc_pass reads only free disk space and mtime but never consults the incrementally-maintained byte_total counter, leaving the store with no size-based reclaim mechanism.

materialize_tickets populates tickets-<sha> entries (~620 MiB each, the largest entries in the store) without calling add_bytes, so ~1.7 GiB of the store's dominant content contributes zero to the byte_total counter that the backstop would rely on.
The missing byte-total trigger and unaccounted materialize_tickets entries combined caused disk pressure on the review-bot host to breach 85% and reach 90% with no eviction firing.
A new configurable max_bytes cap with a default value of 0 (off) must be added to the janitor tunable surface and read by _gc_pass to evict LRU-by-mtime entries when the store exceeds the limit.
materialize_tickets must record its entries in the store's byte total via add_bytes so the incremental counter reflects all entries and agrees with the authoritative walk performed by startup_sweep.
